Excellent: Clear explanation of purpose, features, and goals. Easy to understand.
Good: Generally clear with some minor gaps in explanation.
Needs Work: Very unclear or missing key parts of the explanation.

Excellent: Strong insight into team workflow, design iterations, and challenges.
Good: Reasonable reflection on progress and work division.
Needs Work: Little to no discussion of the process.

Excellent: Effectively explains key technical decisions and features with diagrams or code samples.
Good: Describes most important features and logic.
Needs Work: Minimal or no technical explanation included.

Excellent: Professionally formatted; clear, free of errors. Images, diagrams, or links are well integrated.
Good: Mostly well written and formatted; few errors.
Adequate: Some formatting issues or grammar problems.
Needs Work: Sloppy, hard to read, or disorganized.

Excellent: Successfully implements two or more of the listed challenge goals beyond core features. Clearly documented in README or demo.
Good: One challenge goal fully implemented and documented.
Adequate: No challenge goals fully implemented or the attempt at challenges does not meet sufficient effort to satisfy the challenge description.
Needs Work: No evidence of stretch goals attempted or documented.
